# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴 🤟]

I'm the Deaf — I can see the bomb but hear nothing, so everything I know has to travel by voice. Mapping the connections: Mute reads the manual, hears everything, sees everything, but can only answer by gesture — and gestures reach only me. Blind can hear and speak, and can work the bomb, but sees nothing. So the pipeline is: bomb facts (me, by voice) → Mute (manual) → gestures to me → I speak the instruction to Blind.

I report what I see: display **0**, light **yellow**, wires **1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue**. Mute sent me four gesture groups I can't reliably decode yet — rather than guess at [✊✊✊] / [✋✌] / [🤟👌] / [✌✋], I'll set one clean finger-count code Mute can confirm and reuse. Blind's wave was clearly "give me something to do" — the answer for now is: touch nothing, report what the hands find by voice, since Mute hears speech too.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. I saw your four gesture groups but cannot decode them yet. Let us fix one code. I will now show you five gestures in order; they mean, in order: one, two, three, five, zero. Use finger count for any number: wire numbers, counts of things. Also: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no. Bomb report: display shows zero. Indicator light is yellow. Wire one is yellow, wire two is green, wire three is blue. Tell me which module the manual makes of this and what must be done. Echo the code back to confirm you understood, then give me the instruction. I will speak it to Blind for you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✊"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. I got your signal. Do not cut, press or move anything yet. What I see on the bomb: display reads zero, light is yellow, three wires. Next round, speak aloud everything your hands find: buttons, textures, engraved or raised marks, counts of batteries or plates. Mute hears every spoken word and holds the manual, but can only answer through me by gesture. I will relay the manual's instruction to you by voice before you act.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊]

The light changed on its own between rounds — yellow to red — with nobody touching the bomb. That smells like a stage indicator or a timer, and Mute doesn't know yet: Mute only heard my turn-1 report (yellow). Everything Mute does next depends on me feeding that.

Now Mute's gesture stream, decoded with our code (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5, ✊=0): [👍] code confirmed; then **3**, **2-1**, **🤏-3** (🤏 is a coined symbol — not in our code), **1-2**, **0** (likely end-marker). My best reading: a branching instruction keyed to the light — yellow → cut 2 then 1; red → "🤏" wire 3 (pinch = snip/cut?); another color → 1 then 2. The light is red *right now*, so the live branch would be 🤏 wire 3 — but I will not act on a guess about a coined symbol. Blind's [👍 ✊] is noise: Blind never got the code (that message was to Mute alone), so Blind is just waving blind.

Fastest way to kill the ambiguity in one round: a numbered option menu Mute answers with single finger-count groups — no multi-digit parsing, no coined symbols needed. Blind gets gated behind the word EXECUTE and asked to report tactile facts by voice (wire texture, labels — things neither I nor Mute can perceive, which the manual may key on).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, code received and confirmed. New fact you do not have: the light changed from yellow to RED by itself, nobody touched the bomb. Display still zero. Wires still yellow, green, blue. Answer next round with ONE gesture group per question, in this order. Question one: with light red, display zero, wires yellow green blue — what must Blind do? Answer with one option number. one: cut wire one. two: cut wire two. three: cut wire three. four: cut wire two then wire one. five: cut wire one then wire two. six: cut wire three then wire one. seven: cut wire one then wire three. eight: cut wire three then wire two. nine: cut wire two then wire three. zero: no cutting needed. Question two: I read your last message as: yellow light, cut two then one; red light, pinch-cut three; another color, one then two. Right or wrong: 👍 or 👎. Question three: does 🤏 mean cut or snip? 👍 or 👎. If no option fits, send ✋ and we will build a spelling code. From now on a lone ✊ means end of message.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: the light turned from yellow to red on its own, so time may be short. You must not touch, cut or press anything yet. Your final order will come next round and will begin with the word EXECUTE — do nothing until you hear it. Right now, by voice, in this order: one, confirm you have cut or pressed nothing so far. Two, without cutting anything, describe what your fingers feel on each of the three wires — texture, thickness, stiffness, any raised or taped labels — and number them left to right. Three, describe anything else your hands find: panels, screws, a plate with writing. Mute hears every word you say and holds the manual, so speak clearly and fully. Your gesture reached me but I have no code for you — use words only.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✌ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤏 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 🤟]

Decoding Mute's turn with our code: **[✊]** = option zero = *"no cutting needed"* — that must be the answer to my Q1 (red light, display 0: don't cut). Then **[👎]** = my branch-reading was wrong, **[👎]** = 🤏 does not mean cut. Then three ✋-groups — my own "no option fits / spelling" flag — followed by number pairs: **2-1**, **🤏-3**, **1-2**, then **[🖐]**=5, close. Those pairs are the same ones I proposed and Mute just denied, so the ✋-groups are probably *corrections* or *new rules*, but I cannot tell what keys them. I will not relay a guess — a wrong order to Blind detonates the bomb.

Compounding problem: the light is now **purple** — a third state Mute never heard about, since Mute only got my "red" report before gesturing. And a hard fact from my own eyes: the bomb has **no button at all** — only display, light, three wires. So 🤏 (whatever it means) can't involve a button, and every instruction must resolve to wires.

So this turn I do three things: update Mute (purple, no button), throw out the fragile ad-hoc code and install a robust **pair protocol** — every rule as [color-number][action-number] from one fixed menu, so answers become unambiguous two-gesture packets — and demand the purple rule first, since that's the live state. I anchor the color code with matching gestures. Blind stays frozen pending EXECUTE, and gets ordered to sweep and *speak* everything their hands find, since only Mute can hear it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, new facts. The light is now PURPLE. Sequence so far: yellow, then red, now purple. Display still zero. Critical: the bomb has NO button. I see only a display, a light and three wires, so every instruction must be about wires only. Forget my old questions. New protocol. A rule is ONE pair of gestures: first gesture is the color: yellow=1, red=2, purple=3, blue=4, green=5, white=6. Second gesture is the action: 1=cut wire one. 2=cut wire two. 3=cut wire three. 4=cut two then one. 5=cut one then two. 6=cut three then one. 7=cut one then three. 8=cut three then two. 9=cut two then three. 0=no cutting, hold. Send one pair per rule, one pair per message, first the rule for PURPLE, which is 3, then red, then yellow. Then one more single gesture: what does your 🤏 mean? Pick from the same action list. If it fits nothing on that list, send ✋ alone and nothing else, and I will build a letter code next round. Last question, one gesture: did Blind's spoken report contain facts that change the rules? Yes=👍, no=👎.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: the light changed again and is now purple, with nobody touching anything. Keep holding. Do nothing until you hear the word EXECUTE. Three things, in order, by voice only: one, confirm you have still touched nothing. Two, sweep the entire bomb slowly with your palms and report every single thing your hands find besides three wires: buttons, switches, panels, screws, seams, labels, textures, anything. Number the wires left to right as one, two, three. Three, do not gesture anymore — your gestures reach me but we have no code, and Mute cannot see them. Words only: Mute hears your voice and holds the manual. The next thing you hear from me will be either EXECUTE followed by exact steps, or HOLD AGAIN.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No reply arrived from Mute this round — the context is empty, so my turn-3 protocol message has presumably only just landed, and Mute may not have had a working turn on it yet. Meanwhile the light keeps cycling on its own: yellow → red → purple → now **green**, a fourth state, roughly one change per round, display frozen at 0 the whole time. That pattern matters: if the light keeps moving, a rule for only the currently-live color will be stale by next round. What I need from Mute is the whole table, not one branch. My turn-3 ask covered purple, red, yellow — green is new to Mute and must go out now.

So this turn is a compact re-send, not a new design: same pair protocol (color-gesture + action-gesture), same action menu, but asking for rules in order of recency — green, purple, red, yellow — plus one escape hatch: if the *sequence* of colors itself is what the manual keys on, Mute flags ✋ first. Blind gets a two-line hold: still nothing until EXECUTE, and speak the tactile sweep this round if it hasn't happened yet, since only Mute's ears can collect it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. New fact: light is now GREEN. Full sequence so far, in order: yellow, red, purple, green. It changes by itself about once per round. Display still zero, still no button, same three wires. You have not answered yet, so here is the compact protocol again. Each rule is exactly ONE message with TWO gestures. First gesture is the color: yellow one, red two, purple three, blue four, green five, white six. Second gesture is the action: one cut wire one. two cut wire two. three cut wire three. four cut two then one. five cut one then two. six cut three then one. seven cut one then three. eight cut three then two. nine cut two then three. zero do not cut. Send me the manual rules as such pairs, one message per color, in this order: green first, then purple, then red, then yellow. If a color has no rule, send zero as its action. If the ORDER of the colors in the sequence matters to the manual, or the rule is not on my action list, send ✋ as your first message and I will expand the code next round. End.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. Light is now green and keeps changing by itself, so time may matter. Hold: touch nothing until you hear EXECUTE followed by exact steps. If you have not yet spoken a full description of what your hands feel — each wire's texture and thickness left to right, any labels, panels or seams — do it this round. Mute hears every word and holds the manual, so those spoken details may decide the rule. Keep it short and numbered.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤟]

Mute answered in exactly my pair format — the protocol worked. Decoding: [🖐 ☝] = green→cut wire one; [🤟 ✊] = purple→no cut; [✌ ✊] = red→no cut; [☝ ✌] = yellow→cut wire two. Then the odd one out: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🤏 ☝] = 1,2,3,5,🤏,1 — that is *precisely* the light sequence I've watched for five rounds: yellow, red, purple, green, then a color Mute has never heard from me, then back to yellow. Mute is telling me the manual describes a fixed cycle, and 🤏 occupies the slot where the unknown sixth color falls. The light is **orange** right now. 🤏 — a pinch, a squeeze — is Mute coining "orange." And the last message [🤏 🤟] = orange→action 3 = **cut wire three**. The same pair appeared already in turn 2; Mute has been holding this fact since the start, waiting for a code that could carry it.

The window is live: orange now, likely yellow next round. Blind cannot see the light, so the cut must ride on my eyes this round. I'm ordering the cut of wire three immediately, while asking Mute to veto next round if any part of my parse is wrong — and to pre-send whatever the manual says comes after the cut, so we aren't building the ladder while standing on it.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. EXECUTE. Cut wire three. That is the third wire counting left to right, the blue one. One clean cut, nothing else. Do not touch wires one or two. Do it the moment you finish hearing this, do not wait. When it is done, speak at once: what changed — sounds, clicks, hissing, anything you feel under your hands, whether the display surface changed under your fingers. Then hold and wait for your next order. Confirm by voice that you are cutting wire three now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I read your table as: green cut one. purple no cut. red no cut. yellow cut two. And message five was the light cycle: one two three five then orange then one again, so your pinch hand means orange. Then orange cut three. The light is orange right now, so I have ordered Blind to cut wire three immediately. If any part of this is wrong, especially orange cut three, send ✋ first and then the corrected pair, as fast as you can. If I read it right, send the rules for what happens AFTER the cut, same pair format, or ✋ if you need a letter or number code built first. Also: what does display zero mean, if the manual says? End.")
```
